solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dahlia root, perhaps, in large container here in the middle

parts.note: a tub is a big open container

indicators.note: asks for only the central letters of the word here

explanation.surface: A gardener stores a dahlia root in a big tub right here in the centre of the shed.
explanation.definitionFit: Dahlias grow from swollen underground storage organs, so a dahlia root is an example of this kind of plant part.

clue.text: Cafe has very quickly run low after setback

indicators.note: after joins the pieces in order

parts.note: to tear is to rush along at great speed

indicators.note: setback signals that the next word is set back, written in reverse

parts.note: a cow's low is its moo

explanation.surface: A cafe owner rushes about and runs short of supplies after a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setback' turns MOO into OOM; 'low' is the noise a cow makes, not a level.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea room is a small cafe serving tea and light refreshments.

clue.text: Prepare soldiers? One's clumsy

definitions.meaning: soldiers are strips of toast for dipping in egg, so this is spreading them, butter (verb) and fingers
a clumsy person who keeps dropping things

explanation.surface: An army drill instructor is told that one recruit is clumsy.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'soldiers' are thin fingers of toast dipped into a boiled egg, so the first reading means spread butter on those fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps dropping things is mocked with this exclamation, an idiom for a fumbler.

clue.text: Make friends again with cleric one upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of cleric one are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Patch things up with a priest you have offended.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore friendly relations after a quarrel is the verb's main sense, a synonym.

clue.text: Tense, if sent out to gather flowers originally

indicators.note: the scrambled letters close around another piece, gathering it in
sent out suggests the letters of if sent are scattered and rearranged
points to the opening letter of the word flowers

explanation.surface: Someone tenses up when sent out to pick flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' makes STIFEN from IF SENT, and 'to gather' puts F from 'flowers originally' inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To tense and to stiffen are synonyms as verbs, both meaning to become rigid.

clue.text: Toboggan son used on rocky ridge

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the son letter sits atop the ridge

parts.note: a ledge is a narrow rocky shelf or ridge

explanation.surface: A boy takes his toboggan out on a craggy mountain ridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A sled for sliding down snowy slopes; toboggan and the answer are synonyms.

clue.text: Incense from Scottish church, not the first

indicators.note: the first letter of the church word is dropped

parts.note: kirk is the Scots word for church

explanation.surface: Fragrant smoke drifting from a Scottish church, but not the leading one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incense' looks like the perfumed smoke but is the verb meaning to anger.
explanation.definitionFit: To incense someone is to anger or annoy them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Bold style recycled older fashions

indicators.note: recycled means reprocessed, so the letters of older fashions are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A daring look made by reviving old-fashioned clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Recklessness is a bold, rash manner of behaving, hence a bold style of conduct.

clue.text: Not even one announcer appears regularly

indicators.note: regularly asks for every other letter of the word announcer

explanation.surface: Not a single announcer turns up on a regular basis.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun meaning not any, zero, is exactly not even one.

clue.text: Piece in paper — small piece, not leader

indicators.note: the first letter of the synonym is dropped, its leader removed

parts.note: a particle is a tiny fragment

explanation.surface: A newspaper item described as a small piece without a lead story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not leader' removes the P from PARTICLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A written item in a newspaper is called an article; this is a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Recognised king was victorious over knight

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: over signals that the word is turned back to front

parts.note: won means was victorious
N is the chess abbreviation for knight

explanation.surface: A recognised king won a battle against a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'over' can mean turned back to front; K and N are the chess abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Something recognised is familiar and acknowledged, which is the sense of the adjective here.

clue.text: Orphanage coy about study in the main

indicators.note: about signals the letters of orphanage coy being turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: A shy orphanage resident wonders about studying something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is a poetic term for the sea, so a study in the main is the science of the seas.
explanation.definitionFit: The scientific study of the sea, the main of old poetry, is this discipline.

clue.text: One interested in records finds part of bridge is about six tons

parts.note: an arch is a curved span supporting a bridge

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so is wraps around the six

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A record collector finds a bridge section weighing about six tons.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps and manages historical files and documents works in an archive.

clue.text: Nearly botching small cake

indicators.note: nearly says the synonym is not quite complete, losing its last letter

parts.note: muffing means bungling or botching

explanation.surface: Someone almost ruins a small cake while baking it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' drops the final G of MUFFING.
explanation.definitionFit: A muffin is a small baked item, a kind of little cake or bread roll.

clue.text: Large beetle — such regularly chased by Egyptian, say

indicators.note: chased by puts the second piece after the first, following it
regularly asks for every other letter of the word such

parts.note: an Egyptian is an example of an Arab

explanation.surface: A big beetle of this sort is pursued by an Egyptian.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarab is a large dung beetle held sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Obtain fruit for cases, say

parts.note: to bag something is to get or obtain it
a gage is a plum, as in greengage

explanation.surface: Collecting fruit to be packed into crates.
explanation.definitionFit: Suitcases are examples of travel luggage, hence the 'say' marking an example.

clue.text: Ran around integrated circuit somewhat hot, perhaps

indicators.note: around means the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: sped means ran or rushed

explanation.surface: A microchip that got rather hot after running.
explanation.definitionFit: Food flavoured with chilli or pepper is warm to taste, so hot is one example of it.

clue.text: Daring gain access to power on the way up

parts.note: to enter is to get in or gain access
P is the physics abbreviation for power
rising means climbing or going up

explanation.surface: A daring person gets into power while climbing the ladder.
explanation.definitionFit: Enterprising people show initiative and boldness, so the adjective is a synonym for daring.

clue.text: Left with real estate

parts.note: and means with or plus

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a will with property in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground owned as property is real estate; a synonym.

clue.text: Make small improvements to a motorway before completion

indicators.note: before places the earlier pieces ahead of the last one

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in British roads like the M1
the end is the completion

explanation.surface: Planners tweak a motorway before it is finished.
explanation.definitionFit: To revise something with minor corrections is to alter it slightly, the verb's usual sense.

clue.text: Couple retreating inside boudoir

indicators.note: retreating means going back, so the found letters read upwards in reverse
inside signals letters concealed within the word boudoir

explanation.surface: A pair withdrawing into a lady's private room.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of people, especially performers, form a twosome; couple is a synonym.

clue.text: Illusion created by artist on strike

indicators.note: on puts the artist after the strike word in this across clue

parts.note: a clock chimes when it strikes the hour
RA stands for Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A fantasy is dreamed up by a painter who has downed tools.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is a fanciful dream or delusion, named after the mythical monster.

clue.text: Unpleasant noise in road by dance club

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: a disco is a club for dancing

explanation.surface: A racket in the street next to a nightclub.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, discord is a harsh clash of sounds, so a jarring noise.

clue.text: Sample of potato mostly cut by spades

indicators.note: the shortened word is split open by the next piece
mostly means all but the last letter is used

parts.note: tater is informal slang for potato
S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: A trial portion of potato, largely sliced up by gardening spades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims TATER to TATE, and 'cut by' puts S inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To sample food is to try it, and tasting is exactly that, a verb synonym.
